newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call rates rise, liquidity unevenly spread.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call rates rise, liquidity unevenly spread.

text.p: Dutch call money rates rose on Monday because liquidity was unevenly divided in the market and dealers said some smaller participants, who were short, had to pay a higher rate to a big bank which had surplus liquidity.
They said total liquidity in the market was sufficient, but that its distribution among different players was unbalanced.
"Last week's allocation under the (seven-day) special advances pact was sufficient," said one dealer.
Call money rates rose to a high of 3.25 percent bid from some 3.06 to 3.12 percent bid last Friday.
"It is an interesting situation," said one dealer who said he had managed to make a lot of business from the uneven distribution of liquidity.
Call money rates were bid well above the price of deposits up to three months and briefly surpassed the rate for six-month deposits.
Three month deposits were priced at an unchanged 3.12 percent bid.
The guilder was virtually unchanged, trading at 112.4925 per 100 marks from 112.495 on Friday.
